column1: {{c1::GraphQL}} lets clients request selected fields and related data in a query.
column2:
Flexible selection still requires field and entity authorization.
Review source

column1: Deeply nested GraphQL queries can threaten {{c1::availability}} by consuming excessive resources.
column2:
Configure query limits instead of relying on authentication alone.
Review source

column1: Model Context Protocol lets AI agents discover and call {{c1::tools}}.
column2:
A tool exposes a defined operation rather than granting unrestricted database access.
Review source

column1: {{c1::Prompt injection}} uses untrusted instructions to try to redirect an AI agent's behavior.
column2:
Enforce database access outside the model's prompt instructions.
Review source

column1: Authentication establishes identity. {{c1::Authorization}} determines permitted data and operations.
column2:
An authenticated caller does not automatically receive every permission.
Review source

column1: DAB places authentication configuration under {{c1::runtime.host.authentication}}.
column2:
It is not a separate top-level authentication object.
Review source

column1: DAB's {{c1::EntraID}} provider validates Microsoft Entra JWT bearer tokens.
column2:
AzureAD remains a compatibility name in the documented configuration.
Review source

column1: DAB's JWT {{c1::audience}} identifies the API that the token is intended for.
column2:
The incoming API token and DAB's database connection are separate authentication concerns.
Review source

column1: DAB's JWT {{c1::issuer}} identifies the trusted token issuer.
column2:
Configure the expected tenant issuer rather than accepting arbitrary token issuers.
Review source

column1: With JWT bearer authentication, {{c1::X-MS-API-ROLE}} selects a custom DAB role.
column2:
The requested role must also be present in the token's roles claim.
Review source

column1: A valid bearer-token request without a role-selection header uses DAB's {{c1::Authenticated}} role.
column2:
DAB evaluates one effective role per request.
Review source

column1: To require authentication for a DAB entity, do not grant its read action to {{c1::Anonymous}}.
column2:
Review effective entity permissions rather than relying on the authentication provider alone.
Review source

column1: In DAB 2.0, an unconfigured named role first falls back to {{c1::Authenticated}} permissions for the entity.
column2:
If Authenticated is absent, the fallback is Anonymous.
Review source

column1: DAB controls GraphQL schema discovery with runtime.graphql.{{c1::allow-introspection}}.
column2:
Disabling introspection does not replace entity or field authorization.
Review source

column1: DAB's runtime.graphql.{{c1::depth-limit}} caps query nesting.
column2:
The documented default does not impose a depth limit.
Review source

column1: DAB's runtime.pagination.{{c1::max-page-size}} caps records in one page.
column2:
Multiple pages can still expose many records if the caller is authorized to read them.
Review source

column1: For a DAB table entity, the {{c1::read}} action grants reads without directly granting table writes.
column2:
The wildcard action would also include supported write actions.
Review source

column1: A DAB action's fields.{{c1::include}} lists fields that the action permits.
column2:
Place field restrictions inside the action object.
Review source

column1: A DAB action's fields.{{c1::exclude}} identifies fields that the action must not expose.
column2:
Sensitive fields need authorization restrictions, not just removal from example queries.
Review source

column1: The DAB read policy @item.IsPublic {{c1::eq}} true restricts results to public items.
column2:
The predicate belongs in the read action's policy.database property.
Review source

column1: DAB database policies do not support {{c1::execute}} actions for stored procedures.
column2:
Enforce procedure-specific access checks in the database.
Review source

column1: Before returning customer orders, authorize the trusted caller for the requested {{c1::CustomerID}}.
column2:
A supplied customer identifier does not prove that the caller owns or can access that customer.
Review source

column1: By default, DAB connects to the database using {{c1::its own credentials}}, not the incoming API user's identity.
column2:
Do not assume ORIGINAL_LOGIN() identifies the API's human user.
Review source

column1: SQL MCP Server uses DAB's {{c1::entity permissions}} across its tools.
column2:
MCP access follows the same authorization layer as REST and GraphQL.
Review source

column1: For agent access to database objects, prefer an {{c1::allowlist}} over SQL keyword denylists.
column2:
Text matching does not prove that a generated query stays within permitted operations.
Review source

column1: An MCP agent with permission to execute a stored procedure can perform that procedure's {{c1::write operations}}.
column2:
Disabling direct write tools does not make every callable procedure read-only.
Review source

column1: Apply {{c1::least privilege}} to the database identity used by an API or agent.
column2:
Limit its database rights as well as permissions on the API surface.
Review source

column1: DAB SQL MCP Server's local stdio transport uses the {{c1::Simulator}} authentication provider.
column2:
This is a trusted local workflow rather than remote JWT authentication.
Review source

column1: DAB SQL MCP Server supports {{c1::streamable HTTP}} for standard HTTP hosting.
column2:
Use the server's supported authentication and entity authorization configuration.
Review source

column1: Azure SQL Private Link provides connectivity through {{c1::a private endpoint}} inside a virtual network.
column2:
A public IP firewall allow rule is not a private endpoint.
Review source

column1: After establishing working private connectivity, block public Azure SQL access by disabling {{c1::public network access}}.
column2:
Creating a private endpoint alone does not disable public routing.
Review source

column1: Azure SQL's {{c1::sp_set_firewall_rule}} creates or updates a server-level IP allow rule.
column2:
It does not disable public access or create Private Link connectivity.
Review source

column1: App Service virtual network integration supports {{c1::outbound}} connections from the app.
column2:
It does not make the app's inbound API endpoint private.
Review source

column1: Fabric managed private endpoints give supported workloads {{c1::outbound private access}} to data sources.
column2:
Check workload support instead of assuming every Fabric item supports this feature.
Review source
